activities.title: Capstone Charter: Problem, User, and Bounded Scope

source_resources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
source_resources.author: Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan, Yuan Cao
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Sections 2-4: interleaved reasoning/action protocol; Figure 1 trace format
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Language-model prompting, tool-call loops, and basic action/observation traces.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary literature for interleaving explicit reasoning steps with bounded tool actions; anchors the capstone's requirement that every step produces an inspectable observation inside a budgeted loop.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv; conference version hosted on OpenReview.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The curriculum restates the action/observation loop and reimplements a deterministic three-tool agent locally; no paper text is imported.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Wei et al.: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Pure reasoning traces without tool actions; ReAct adds the observable action/observation protocol that the capstone harness enforces.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Huang et al.: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Embodied closed-loop planning for robotics; ReAct's text-domain tool protocol maps directly onto the capstone's bounded tools.

source_resources.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
source_resources.author: Margaret Mitchell, Simone Wu, Andrew Zaldivar, Parker Barnes, Lucy Vasserman, Ben Hutchinson, Elena Spitzer, Inioluwa Deborah Raji, Timnit Gebru
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic model evaluation vocabulary: dataset, metric, intended use.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standard framework for disclosing a model's intended use, evaluation conditions, and limitations; supplies the capstone's model-choice and provenance documentation pattern.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv and in the ACM digital library.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The curriculum provides a local model-decision table template covering intended use, evaluation data, and caveats.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Gebru et al.: Datasheets for Datasets
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Dataset-side documentation rather than model-side; used alongside Model Cards in the provenance table rather than as a replacement.
Vendor-specific safety disclosure; Model Cards provide the general reusable schema.

activities.title: Acceptance Contract: Fixed Tasks, Baseline, and Ceilings

source_resources.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
source_resources.author: Xiao Liu, Hao Yu, Hanchen Zhang, Yifan Xu, Xuanyu Lei, Hanyu Lai, Yu Gu, Hangliang Ding, Kaiwen Men, Kejuan Yang, et al.
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 4.1 Evaluation Setup and Section 4.3 Analysis
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Agent loops, tool use, and benchmark design fundamentals.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Systematic multi-environment agent benchmark; supplies the capstone's fixed-task-set discipline and per-task scoring decomposition used by the acceptance contract.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv; benchmark code and data on GitHub under their own license.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The capstone task set is fixed locally in the acceptance contract and does not require downloading the benchmark.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Zhou et al.: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Deep single-domain web tasks with hosted infrastructure; AgentBench's multi-environment view better fits a general agent evaluation.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Mialon et al.: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Assistant-level real-world questions; also cited by the capstone for outcome-level task design.

source_resources.title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
source_resources.author: Gregoire Mialon, Clementine Fourrier, Craig Swift, Thomas Wolf, Yann LeCun, Thomas Scialom
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Sections 3-4: level design, tooling requirements, human vs agent gap
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Agent capabilities, tool use, and evaluation metrics.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Defines graded assistant tasks with unambiguous factual scoring; motivates the capstone's distinction between success tasks, malformed-request handling, and failure cases.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv; question set hosted on Hugging Face with its own terms.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The capstone evaluation tasks are defined in the local acceptance contract and need no external download.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Liu et al.: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Multi-environment execution benchmark; GAIA adds graded real-world assistance tasks, and both inform the fixed task taxonomy.
Web-only task environment; GAIA covers general assistant capability beyond browsing.

source_resources.author: Timnit Gebru, Jamie Morgenstern, Briana Vecchione, Jennifer Wortman Vaughan, Hanna Wallach, Hal Daumé III, Kate Crawford
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 3 Questions and Workflow (3.1 Motivation through 3.7 Maintenance)
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Dataset provenance, splits, and licensing vocabulary.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standard questionnaire for documenting dataset origin, composition, rights, and maintenance; structures the capstone evidence package's data-provenance table.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv and in the ACM digital library.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The provenance table template in the capstone instructions restates the required disclosure fields locally.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Mitchell et al.: Model Cards for Model Reporting
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Model-side reporting rather than dataset-side; the capstone provenance table cites both.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Bender & Friedman: Data Statements for Natural Language Processing
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: NLP-specific demographic disclosure; Datasheets cover the general lifecycle needed for arbitrary capstone data.
